This petition has been filed by the applicant under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of entire criminal proceedings under Section 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of POCSO Act in connection with Criminal Case No. SC. 06/2021 which is arising out of crime No. 120/2020 Police Station Karahiya District Gwalior pending before 4th ASJ Gwalior (M.P.) on the basis of compromise.

During pendency of this petition, the applicant and the complainant had filed the application alongwith their affidavits which were registered as IA No.8970/2023 and stating that they have Bhola Alias Pankaj Shakya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135132653/

sentences.text: T his Court, vide order dated 11.05.223, had directed the parties to appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court for recording their statements and for verification of factum of compromise.
The Principal Registrar has submitted his report on 15.05.2023 itself and verified the compromise.

In the cases of Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another (AIR 2008 SC 1968),
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab (AIR 2008 SC 1969), Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another (2011)
10 SCC 705, and Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, Anita Maria Dias and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Anr. (2018) 3 SCC 290, Supreme Court has laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the court can be saved and utilized in other material cases.

sentences.text: After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and taking into account the law laid down by the Apex Court, in the opinion of this court, continuance of the prosecution in such matters will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Under such a situation, section 482 Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.
Moreso, the offence in question is not against the society but merely affects the victim.

Consequent upon the above said facts and that the accused applicant and the complainant have amicably resolved the issue and they are permitted to compound the offences, this Court allows this MCRC with the following directions :-
Entire criminal proceedings under Section 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of POCSO Act in connection with Criminal Case No. SC. 06/2021 which is arising out of crime No. 120/2020 Police Station Karahiya District Gwalior pending before 4th ASJ Gwalior (M.P. are hereby quashed.
The applicant is discharged from the charges of the present case on the basis of compromise.
The petition, accordingly, stands allowed.
Certified copy as per rules.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the cases of Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another (AIR 2008 SC 1968),
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab (AIR 2008 SC 1969), Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another (2011)
10 SCC 705, and Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, Anita Maria Dias and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Anr. (2018) 3 SCC 290, Supreme Court has laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the court can be saved and utilized in other material cases.
After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and taking into account the law laid down by the Apex Court, in the opinion of this court, continuance of the prosecution in such matters will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Under such a situation, section 482 Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.
Moreso, the offence in question is not against the society but merely affects the victim.
